title: Monetary Policy Report—July 2025
summary: The Bank of Canada released its July 2025 Monetary Policy Report maintaining the overnight rate target at 2.75%, with inflation near the 2% target but underlying price pressures rising to about 2½%. The report highlights significant US tariff increases since early 2025 and considerable uncertainty around trade policy as key factors weighing on the Canadian economic outlook.
key_points: Bank of Canada held target overnight rate at 2¾% (Bank Rate at 3%, deposit rate at 2.70%)
Headline inflation near 2% target but underlying inflation has risen to approximately 2½%
Canadian economic activity slowed considerably due to trade conflict but showing signs of resilience
US tariffs significantly higher than at start of 2025; trade policy remains unpredictable
Global growth has slowed since early 2025 amid US trade policy shifts and resulting uncertainty
Range of trade policy outcomes has narrowed with some new tariff agreements in place, but situation remains fluid
why_it_matters: This quarterly monetary policy report from the Bank of Canada provides the official institutional view on Canada's economic outlook and inflation trajectory. The 2.75% rate hold signals cautious policy amid elevated uncertainty from US trade actions. Rising underlying inflation to 2½% while headline sits at 2% suggests persistent price pressures that could complicate future rate decisions. The report's scenario assumptions and risk assessments inform market expectations for Bank of Canada policy path.
macro_context: The report identifies US tariffs and trade policy uncertainty as the primary risks to the Canadian economic outlook. Global growth has slowed but remained resilient despite tariffs being at highest levels in decades. Underlying inflation picking up to 2½% while headline inflation holds near 2% suggests second-round effects from tariffs may be materializing. The Bank's scenario horizon shows inflation remaining close to target over the projection period.
